name: sales_pitch
hook: I gave this pitch a live hype meter.

questions.label: Concrete metric
questions.instructions: Does `sentence` give a concrete, measurable number about the product or business?

true.means: Users, revenue, retention, time saved, price, speed with an actual figure.
examples: From nine days to under four hours.

false.means: Claims of traction or quality without a figure.

questions.label: Buzzwords
questions.instructions: Is `sentence` mostly buzzwords with little concrete meaning?

true.means: Stacked jargon like AI-native, next-gen, disruptive, synergy, paradigm with no concrete function.
examples: An AI-native platform synergizing next-gen workflows.

false.means: It says concretely what the product does, even if it mentions AI or cloud.
examples: It flags duplicate vendor charges in your bank statements.
A small model labels tickets by urgency.

questions.label: Overpromise
questions.instructions: Does `sentence` promise results that are too good to be true or unbacked?

true.means: Guaranteed dramatic outcomes, absolute promises, total elimination of problems.
examples: We guarantee revenue triples in 90 days.
You'll never think about taxes again.

false.means: Typical ranges, honest limits, certifications or modest claims.
examples: Customers typically see a 15 to 25 percent drop.
It won't fix a bad product.

questions.label: Urgency pressure
questions.instructions: Does `sentence` pressure the listener with artificial urgency or scarcity?

true.means: Deadlines, limited spots, fear of missing out, 'sign today'.
examples: Only three slots left, sign today.

false.means: Neutral timelines, invitations to take time, or plain availability.
examples: Take a couple of weeks with the trial.

questions.label: Vague benefit
questions.instructions: Does `sentence` describe a benefit so vaguely that it cannot be checked?

true.means: Benefits like better lives, unlocked potential, new levels of clarity.
examples: It makes your team's life so much better.

false.means: A specific, checkable benefit: time saved, a named feature, a removed manual task.
examples: It saves six hours of data entry a week.
Reps stop copying call notes by hand.
